thread.title: Now Is The Time To Buy HP - HP Inc. (NYSE:HPQ)

author: StockBot
title: Now Is The Time To Buy HP - HP Inc. (NYSE:HPQ)
text:
Source: HP
Ever since splitting with Hewlett Packard Enterprises (NYSE: HPE ) back in November 2015, HP ( HPQ ) has had quite a solid performance. Its stock price has surged 57.9 percent since then, outpacing the Nasdaq's 46.2 percent gain over the same period.
In addition to this, HP has beaten analysts estimates in the last three quarters and continues to steadily grow its revenue across its core business segments. Back in 2016, the management had stated that it intended to stabilize revenue by 2017 and succeeded in doing this one quarter earlier than expected.
HP had an impressive FY2017, growing revenue by 8 percent year-over-year, and this year seems to be off to a great start with Q1 revenue increasing 14 percent YoY to $14.5 billion and earnings coming it $0.48 per share, a 16 percent increase from the year-ago period.
While Personal Systems revenue delivered strong growth, up 15 percent YoY to $9.4 billion for the quarter, operating margin dipped 20 basis points to 3.7 percent driven by DRAM component cost gains. In addition to this, the acquisition of Samsung's ( OTC:SSNLF ) Print business further exerted margin pressure on the Print segment which caused operating margin to decline by 80 basis points sequentially to 15.8 percent.
Looking at its bread and butter - the PC business, HP has been able to make significant gains in the market. At the beginning of last year, the company became the world's leading PC manufacturer taking the top spot away from China's Lenovo ( OTCPK:LNVGY ).
Interestingly, while global PC unit shipments only rose 0.7 percent in 4Q2017, HP grew its shipments by an impressive 8.3 percent during the same period, ending up with 23.5 percent of the market share according to figures from International Data Corporation (IDC). During the first-quarter earnings presentation, management reiterated that it was confident about achieving YoY PC unit shipment growth in 2018 thanks to product innovation.
Catalysts for growth A recent press release by HP further describes why a bright future lies ahead for the company. Conservatively speaking, the company believes that the total available market across its strategic business segments is worth about $560 billion, with approximately $300 billion being in its core printing and personal systems segments.
Going forward, management has indicated that its focus will be finding pockets of opportunity and growth within these strategic segments in order to drive growth. Bearing this in mind, here are some of the areas the company is keen on to catalyze growth:
3D printing: Thanks to the numerous advancements in 3D printing technology, plenty of use cases in industrial, automotive, and real estate sectors have emerged and HP couldn't be in a better position to take advantage of the massive opportunity here. Just how big is the opportunity? HP estimates that it could be north of $12 trillion and it expects that its Multi Jet Fusion technology will take care of customer concerns which include cost, speed, and quality.
Source: HP investor presentation
Although there is undeniable competition in the space from other players such as Stratasys (NASDAQ: SSYS ), Faro Technologies (NASDAQ: FARO ), and Materialise (NASDAQ: MTLS ), HP has a major competitive edge. According to the company, its technology is ten times faster than and halves the cost of printing in comparison to other 3D printing technologies. In addition to this, HP also has the only multicolor 3D printer system and plans to expand into 3D metals market.
Desktop-as-a-service (DaaS): This is another revenue driver that HP intends to take full advantage of. Basically, DaaS is a cloud-based model which enables users to work from any location using their devices to access a software application. Recently, the company announced that it had entered an agreement with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) to manage its iOS and Mac devices for selected customers indicating the increasing appeal of the service as a means of reducing costs to businesses.
Workspace-as-a-service (WaaS) which includes DaaS is expected to grow from $4.8 billion in 2014 to at least $13.45 billion by 2022 according to research from MarketsandMarkets , and HP is confident that this offering will translate to a high margin business that will generate revenue from both services and devices.
A3 copiers: HP is making a huge bet on the A3 copier market which it believes could drive revenue even higher. The company's acquisition of Samsung's printing business for $1.1 billion which completed in November last year aims to give it enough momentum to go after the A3 copier market. The total addressable market here is estimated to be worth $55 billion and HP believes it could disrupt this market thanks to its differentiated laser printing technology.
The company reported that it is aiming for about 12 percent market share in this segment by 2020 compared to its current 7.9 percent share of the market. To achieve this, HP has revealed that it has plans to penetrate the A3 market in every country over the next couple of years. In 1Q2018, HP's printing segment reported 14 percent YoY revenue growth to $5.1 billion on the backdrop of supplies and commercial hardware sales growth.
Now what? With second quarter earnings expected to be released before the end of this week, the only weak link that shareholders should be on the lookout for is DRAM prices. Higher DRAM prices as a result of increasing commodity prices negatively impacted HP's earnings last year, and if this persists, it could pose a major challenge for the company. The only way out of this predicament according to HP will be to pass on the component price increase to consumers which could lower demand.
In case you may be wondering how HP has treated its shareholders so far, here is what you need to know. Last year, the company returned 69 percent of its $3.3 billion in free cash flow to shareholders in the form of share buybacks and dividends.
During the company's recent annual meeting CEO Dion Weisler noted:
We will continue to be disciplined with capital allocation. In this business, our capital expenditure requirements are modest, and we will determine all of our investments against a returns-based framework. Our current strategy is to return 50 to 70 percent of free cash flow to shareholders.
HP's dividend yield of 2.5 percent is better than Western Digital's (NYSE: WDC ) 2.3 percent and lower than Seagate's (NASDAQ: STX ) 4.4 percent.
Its shares also don't appear to be expensive at current levels. The company said it expects fiscal 2018 earnings per share to come in around $2.00, up from $1.81 which would maintain the PE under 10X.
At the moment, HP's financial position seems solid with cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter of $5.4 billion and a $1.2 billion net debt position, which includes approximately $1 billion in funding for S-Print.
Conclusion HP is undoubtedly well positioned to take advantage of multiple opportunities as the catalysts mentioned above illustrate. Taking into account its conservative estimates of the value of these opportunities combined with its reasonable valuation, HP should be a worthy consideration for any long-term investor out there.
